items.title: Ask HN: Are we putting pricing on things too quickly?
items.snippet: I'm an early adopter. I genuinely enjoy exploring new ideas and trying early-stage products. But lately, when I browse launch platforms, even SideProject subreddit, it feels like almost everything is behind a paywall. Some offer a free trial, but I more often see posts saying something was vibe-coded in a few hours, and yet it costs over $50 to use. What feel odd to me is this: They are asking people for feedback. items.title: Ask HN: Building KasirCepat, an offline-first POS for Indonesia
items.snippet: I'm building KasirCepat, a POS application for small shops in Indonesia. Many of these businesses have unreliable internet connections, so I started with a local-first architecture instead of cloud-first. The main goal is to make the daily workflow simple: - selling products, - tracking inventory, - viewing sales history. I'm curious how other developers approach: - data synchronization, - multi-device workflows, - handling conflicts, - designing software for non-technical users. Especially interested in lessons from building local-first/offline-first applications.

items.title: feat(saas-ops): painel de pools de cobrança (Boleto Cloud) com consumo por cliente
items.snippet: ## Contexto O Boleto Cloud cobra por **conta**, pelo total de boletos únicos criados no mês, em faixas progressivas. A regra de excedente de faixa **não está clara** (a FAQ fala em "faixa superior ou proporcional"). Enquanto o volume cresce, alocar todos os clientes numa conta única pode cair no "penhasco" de faixa (1.000 → 5.000 = R$ 310 → R$ 1.400). Estratégia aprovada (ver #362): **pools de cobrança** — grupos de clientes distribuídos entre contas para aproveitar a faixa com headroom, migrando de faixa só quando o custo incremental compensar. ## Escopo Tudo no **control-plane (admin-center/SaaS Ops)** — a instância do cliente só recebe a configuração da conta/beneficiário. ### Dados/migra

items.title: Received credit note: post it against its bill from the inbox, reversing VAT from 1135 before 1130
items.snippet: ## Goal A received credit note (type E, TipoRelacion 01 or 03) related to one bill is booked against it from the inbox, and its VAT leaves where the bill's VAT sits: 1135 up to what is still parked, 1130 for the rest (LIVA arts. 5 fr. III and 7). ## Tranche and context - **Tranche:** new, named in #693's Out of scope and by the 13 Nov audit (`docs/auditorias/2026-11-13-contra-el-objetivo/hallazgos.json:445-453`). - **Why now** (`develop` `fe702017`, read, not run): - **The rule is wrong.** `egreso_recibido_nota_credito` credits `iva_acreditable` whatever the bill did (`src/services/xml-ingestion/cfdi-taxonomy.ts:305`), though its note says a PPD's reversal «must go against that same account»

items.title: [UI] Live PAC test (spec 076): re-run after mbe-api#349
items.snippet: Follow-up to #288 (spec 076, task T014). This is blocked on mictlanix/mbe-api#349. The live test `test/integration/fiscal_documents_live_test.dart` ran on dev on 2026-11-19, with the simulator on and `MBE_WRITE=true`. It passed 50 of 51 steps: | Group | Result | |---|---| | Facturas | 19/19 | | 072 stamp, cancel and refresh | 10/11 | | 073 credit note | 8/8 | | 074 payment receipt | 13/13 | The failing step is `B: cancel again, the receiver accepts, refresh: cancelled with two entries, newest first`. Its scenario: after the receiver rejected a pending cancellation, the same document is cancelled again. mbe-api closes that second request as `rejected` at once, against SAT's earlier rejection.
